title: A novelist who brings a new character in through a scene's active fallout lets the existing consequence chain carry the arrival without separate exposition
body:
- A chapter already shaped by a triggering event's ripple effects naturally accommodates a new character whose own motivation is responding to that event.
- The triggering event supplies both the character's reason for appearing and the stakes of their interaction, so no separate exposition is needed.
- The thematic coherence of the chapter's existing consequence chain absorbs the new arrival and lets the introduction advance the chapter rather than interrupt it.
- Case: A chapter titled "First Consequences" that shows ripple effects from a viral video naturally accommodates new characters responding to that event.
conversion: none — standing condition: a triggering event's continuing fallout can carry a new character into the scene without separate exposition, sparing the novelist the interruption a standalone arrival would otherwise demand
